slides.heading: Binary Tree Diameter
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Binary Tree Diameter, a medium binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: The longest path through a node joins the heights of its two subtrees.
slides.narration: The longest path through a node joins the heights of its two subtrees.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: diameter through each node via separate height calls → O(n²)
Post-order computing height once per node → O(n)
Diameter need not pass through the root
slides.narration: Computing heights separately for every node repeats work and is quadratic. A single post-order pass returns each subtree's height and, along the way, checks the path that bends through each node.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. At each node, left height plus right height is a candidate
slides.narration: Step by step. First, post-order returns each subtree's height. Second, at each node, left height plus right height is a candidate. Third, track the maximum.

slides.caption: At 8: left 1 + right 0 = 1; best 1
slides.narration: At node 8, the left height is 1 and the right height is 0. A path through here has 1 edges. Best so far: 1.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Height returns zero for null. It computes left and right heights, updates the best diameter with their sum, and returns one plus the larger height.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Longest path may avoid the root
slides.narration: The diameter counts edges, and it often doesn't pass through the root, as in this example.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Return height, track best in a field/array
slides.narration: Return the height and track the best in a shared variable. The hard follow-up maximises path sum instead of length.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: The longest path through a node joins the heights of its two subtrees.
slides.narration: To recap Binary Tree Diameter: The longest path through a node joins the heights of its two subtrees. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
